Asks this week:

- Infra (Karthik): flag any capacity conflicts in us-west-2 for the Target scenario and suggest short-term mitigations (burst slots, regional routing).
- Monica: help align commercial canaries / rollout phasing for Atlas so we can sequence reserve capacity.

Plan: let's tie this out on Wednesday, May 12 at 11:00 PT (30 min). If that works for Atlas, Brian, please confirm. I'll circulate a short MCA (attached draft "MCA_AtlasHealth_v2.pdf") after the call with committed metrics and milestones.

Thanks for the workbook, good layout. Quick finance read:
- Conservative: assumes 30% of early deals convert in Q3; monthly burn estimate aligns with our standard seat/slot conversion in column H. Calendarized revenue looks OK for applying the trial credit through July.
- Target: pushes ~2.1M in incremental usage into Aug/Sept and would require an elevated reserved-commitment profile for two months (we can cover via a short-term credit and amortize).
- Aggressive: needs a formal review with FP&A — I flagged rows 42-47 where the surge causes a 40% month-over-month burn increase.

Action items from finance side:
1) I'll add a "credit amortization" tab to the workbook by EOD Tuesday so infra has a clearer sense of committed dollars tied to each slot tranche.
2) Please make sure the MCA includes the exact milestone dates for when credit applies (we need the timing to match revenue recognition rules).

Ben / all —

Quick infra read after skimming the workbook: good fidelity on token->slot mapping. A few infra constraints and mitigation suggestions:

Constraints:
- us-west-2 pool: Target scenario consumes ~78% of available reserved slots in week 34 (row 58). If other enterprise deals ramp, we risk hitting soft limits on model variants that require A100 class nodes.
- Burst capacity: limited by supply windows in early Aug; procurement lead time for spot pools could be 6-8 weeks.

Mitigations:
1) Regional routing: shift non-latency-bound workloads to us-east-1 for weeks 33-36; we have spare ephemeral capacity there.
2) Canary plan: recommend a phased canary for Atlas where we reserve 20% of the Target slot count for week 1, then scale to full Target after SLA telemetry is green.
3) Quantization / model mapping: for the aggressive tail, consider a 4-bit quantized variant that reduces slot pressure by ~30% for embedding-heavy pipelines — need SAR approval.

I'll add inline comments to the workbook with cell-level notes (capacity_risk? flag in column J). Monica — can you confirm the proposed canary sequencing and whether Sales wants that reflected in the MCA milestones?

Karthik Iyer
Director, Infrastructure — Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com | (415) 555-0174
